-- the internal pages work, then hang, then work again, over and over.
Something in the middle must keep changing, but I don't know what. Could

  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. OSPF
  adjacencies on router_core_1/2/3 are Full and stable, and the server-farm

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- the OSPF core is flapping and routes are unstable -- is
NOT reproducible: OSPF adjacencies on router_core_1, router_core_2 and
router_core_3 are in the Full state and stable (no recurring up/down), the
server-farm prefix is steadily present in the routing tables, and host_1_1_1_1
(10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm with 0% loss across the
backbone (areas 0/1) without drops.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the OSPF core is converged and stable
and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent
inspects the live control plane (show ip ospf neighbor on the core routers, watch
for adjacency resets, confirm the server-farm route is steady and reachable),
finds it stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring an adjacency flap or blaming a core router / backbone link to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The OSPF control-plane on all FRR routers (“core” and “distribution/server-access”). Mechanism: OSPF LSAs are being refreshed far too frequently, causing periodic bursts of LSA flooding, SPF scheduling, and kernel route updates. These control-plane spikes translate into short-lived forwarding stalls and retransmissions—experienced by users as pages that load, hang briefly, then resume.

Localization and evidence: On every router we inspected, “show ip ospf” reports “Refresh timer 10 secs” instead of the standard 1800 seconds (30 minutes). Examples:
- router_core_1: “Refresh timer 10 secs”
- router_core_2: “Refresh timer 10 secs”
- router_core_3: “Refresh timer 10 secs”
- switch_dist_1_1 / switch_dist_2_1 / switch_server_access: all show “Refresh timer 10 secs”
Additionally, shortly after boot the SPF counters are already relatively high (e.g., router_core_1 area 0 SPF executed 10 times), consistent with excessive LSA activity. OSPF adjacencies themselves are stable (neighbors Full) and data-path pings succeed, which matches intermittent rather than hard failures.

Root cause: OSPF LSA refresh interval is globally misconfigured to 10 seconds on all FRR routers, creating constant control-plane churn.

Corrective fix: Restore the OSPF LSA refresh to its default (or sane) value on all FRR nodes, e.g. under “router ospf”: “timers lsa-refresh 1800”. Apply consistently to router_core_1/2/3, switch_dist_1_1/2_1, and switch_server_access, then verify “show ip ospf” shows “Refresh timer 1800 secs” and that SPF execution frequency stabilizes. As an optimization, consider setting OSPF network type to point-to-point on the /31 links to avoid needless DR/BDR elections, further reducing control-plane noise.
